title: Route policy: add quantization enablement + canary percentage with precedence + config migrations
author: Benji Okafor
description: Summary: This PR adds route-level quantization enable/disable and deterministic canary percentage gating to the policy engine. It also introduces explicit precedence rules (org default -> customer override -> route override) and a config migration path from the legacy model-scoped quantization flag to the new route-scoped settings. Motivation: Quantization Profile Library is opt-in and needs safety controls that let customers roll out quantized execution on specific workloads/routes (e.g., background summarization) without affecting interactive chat. Canary gating + clear precedence lets us do staged rollouts and fast rollback without bespoke per-customer codepaths. Details: Adds new policy inputs: route.quantization.mode (inherit|enabled|disabled) and route.quantization.canary_percent (0-100, only applied when mode resolves to enabled). Adds customer-level override (customer.quantization.mode/canary_percent) and org default (org.quantization.mode/canary_percent). Precedence rules: route setting wins over customer, customer wins over org. 'inherit' means fall through to the next layer; if all inherit/unset, default is disabled. Canary evaluation: when resolved mode is enabled and canary_percent < 100, quantization is enabled for a deterministic subset of requests using stable hashing over (route_id, customer_id, request_id) to avoid per-worker skew and allow consistent behavior during retries. Migrations: Reads legacy config key quantization.enabled (model-scoped) and maps it to org.quantization.mode=enabled for backward compatibility when route/customer/org keys are absent. Emits a structured warning in config validation to encourage migration; no behavior change intended for existing tenants unless they set route/customer overrides. Validation: Adds schema validation ensuring canary_percent is integer [0,100] and disallows canary_percent when mode resolves to disabled at the same layer (e.g., explicit disabled + canary set). Also adds a guard to treat missing request_id as non-canary (baseline) unless canary_percent == 100 (prevents accidental high-variance sampling for clients that don’t pass request ids). Observability hooks: Adds decision tags to the policy evaluation result (quantization_decision: baseline|quantized, quantization_reason: disabled|inherit_disabled|canary_drop|canary_pass|enabled_100) for downstream metrics (full metrics tagging comes in a follow-up PR). Rollout: Gated behind feature flag policy.quantization_route_controls (default off). When off, legacy behavior remains unchanged. Test plan: Unit tests for precedence resolution matrix, canary hash distribution sanity (0/50/100), and migration behavior when legacy key is present. Integration tests exercising routing->policy->decision object with mixed org/customer/route configs. Manual: Used /internal/policy/eval with sample configs for FinchAI-style workload (summarization route enabled at 10% canary; chat route disabled). Notes/Follow-ups: Audit log + Console API wiring is in PR 28861. Runtime compatibility fallback is in PR 28805. Metrics tagging is in PR 28833.
commits: policy: introduce QuantizationMode enum + resolved quantization decision in policy output
config: add org/customer/route quantization config keys + schema validation
policy: deterministic canary gate using stable hash over request identity
migration: map legacy quantization.enabled -> org.quantization.mode for backcompat
tests: precedence matrix + canary distribution + integration coverage
docs(internal): update policy config examples for quantization route controls
review_conversation: Jordan Lee (review): The precedence rules look right, but I’m worried about canary stability across retries. If request_id is missing or changes, we might flip-flop between baseline and quantized and make debugging impossible. Can we (a) require request_id for canary < 100, or (b) define a fallback key? Benji Okafor (author): Agree. I added a guard: if canary_percent < 100 and request_id is missing, we default to baseline and add quantization_reason=canary_missing_request_id. For canary_percent == 100 we still enable to avoid breaking folks who want always-on for a route but don’t pass ids. Mina Haddad (review): Please confirm the hashing uses route_id and customer_id as salt so we don't correlate canary cohorts across routes (we want to be able to canary a single route without inadvertently enabling the same users everywhere). Benji Okafor (author): Updated in 7c2a1f1 to hash(route_id|customer_id|request_id). Added test that two routes with same request_id do not produce identical canary decisions distributionally. Ravi Menon (review): Migration: mapping legacy quantization.enabled to org default seems okay, but we should avoid silently changing behavior when someone sets route/customer to inherit. If they set route=inherit explicitly, do we still pick up legacy? Benji Okafor (author): Yes—inherit falls through and will still land on org layer; legacy mapping only populates org defaults when org keys are absent. Added a config validation warning: 'legacy quantization.enabled is deprecated; set org.quantization.mode explicitly'. Ethan Park (review): The schema currently allows canary_percent when mode=disabled at the same layer, but it will be ignored after resolution. Prefer to fail validation to avoid confusing config. Benji Okafor (author): Done. Validation now rejects canary_percent set alongside explicit disabled at the same layer. Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Please add at least one integration test that shows feature flag off preserves existing outputs. We need safety for staged rollout. Benji Okafor (author): Added integration test: policy.quantization_route_controls=false => quantization_decision always baseline and no new fields emitted. Jordan Lee (final): LGTM after the request_id guard + validation change. Mina Haddad (final): Approved. Ravi Menon (final): Approved.
release_notes: Internal: Policy engine now supports route-level quantization enable/disable with deterministic canary gating and explicit org/customer/route precedence (behind feature flag policy.quantization_route_controls).
